sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the commercial centre of Rahway at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right. Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet from East and West Milton Avenue at the left edge to its bend toward Monroe Street at the right, lined on both sides by two- and three-storey brick and frame stores: drug stores, a bakery, a hardware and paints store, the Lyric Theatre, and the City Offices near the east end. Cherry Street runs north from Main between solid rows of stores to Irving Street, where the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks and yard cross the top of the sheet. Lewis Street cuts through the blocks on either side of Main and jogs slightly where it crosses it. In the upper left block, west of Lewis, stand the Rahway Trust Company, Irving Inn, a plumbing supply store and Trinity M.E. Church, with dwellings on the side streets; a bank, a Western Union office and insurance offices stand on Irving Street. South of Main, Augusta Street divides the residential blocks along West and East Milton Avenue and Lewis Street from the commercial frontage. Dock Street follows the west bank of the Rahway River in the lower right, with the river drawn in blue; the shore is lined with small stores, a bakery supply store and a few dwellings. Water pipes are lettered along the streets, with the street widths of 56, 66 and 70 feet noted. Neighbouring sheets 3, 4, 5, 8, 10 and 23 are indicated in the margins.
notes: West Milton Avenue and East Milton Avenue are one street, East Milton Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Cherry is East Cherry Street.
Lewis Street is drawn offset where it crosses Main (the northern part lies about 19 feet west of the southern part); only its southern junctions were used.
Vail Place (lettered sideways at upper left, V read with medium confidence) is not in OpenStreetMap.
Map, 50 ft. Downtown east of Irving: Main, Lewis, Cherry, Monroe, Poplar, Dock, Augusta, Milton, Rahway River. One part. Lewis drawn offset north of Main.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the district south-west of the centre of Rahway at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right. The sheet is crossed diagonally by the broad Pennsylvania Railroad right-of-way, drawn as many parallel tracks, which separates the blocks of Georgia, Clinton and Broad Streets at the top from the lower blocks. In the upper blocks, small frame dwellings face Clinton Street and a pink brick garage and auto sales building stands at the right. Below the tracks, Fulton Street and Pierce Street run across the sheet from Commerce Street at the left to West and East Milton Avenue at the right. Between them lie closely built lots of frame dwellings with a lumber company, the Rahway Lumber Co. with lumber sheds and piles and a sawing and planing mill, a Moose Home, a repair shop and auto sales and service buildings. South of Pierce Street, the blocks reach Main Street at the bottom edge, with dwellings, a brick storage building, a long dwelling row and several auto sales and repair buildings. New Brunswick Avenue and Haydock Street enter at the bottom. Water pipes are shown in nearly every street and street widths of 60 and 66 feet are noted. Neighbouring sheets 2, 4, 10, 11, 15 and 26 are indicated in the margins.
notes: West Milton Avenue and East Milton Avenue are one street, East Milton Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Commerce is East Emerson Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Haydock Street is not in OpenStreetMap.
Broad Street and Clinton Street meet at the tracks, but that junction fell 17 m from the fit and was not used.
Map, 50 ft. Broad, Clinton, Georgia, Fulton, Commerce (East Emerson Avenue), Pierce, Milton, Main, Irving, New Brunswick Av. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north-west edge of the centre of Rahway at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north points almost to the right. Esterbrook Avenue runs along the top edge, with West Milton Avenue at the left, Cherry in the middle and Elm Avenue at the right, all drawn at 60 or 66 feet with water pipes. The upper left blocks are lots of frame dwellings. In the centre stands the Monte Christi Corp., bleachers and dyers of straw braids and body hats, with its bleach houses, dye house and a large tank, and to the left the Regina Corp., makers of vacuum cleaners, a large brick factory with a garage, show room and park beside it. Campbell Street crosses the middle of the sheet from Cherry to Elm Avenue. Below it stand Cross Keys Inn, an auto laundry and The Elm Apartments and, in the right-hand blocks along Irving Street, the Rahway Record, F.C. Bauer's candy and ice cream factory, the Rahway Savings Institution, a Sunday school auditorium and St. Paul Episcl. Church. The Pennsylvania Railroad passes diagonally across the lower left with its depot, steel frame platform sheds and conc. platforms; below it are the Rahway National Bank and a row of stores on Irving Street. Neighbouring sheets 2, 3, 5, 15 and 18 are indicated in the margins.
notes: West Milton Avenue is West Milton Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Cherry is West Cherry Street, and the lower Cherry Street is East Cherry Street. Farrell Place is part of Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
Campbell Street ends at Cherry on this sheet although OpenStreetMap continues it to Broad Street; that modern junction was left out.
Broad Street and West Cherry Street was accepted at Farrell Place with a residual of 3 m (medium confidence).
Map, 50 ft. Downtown at the PRR station: Esterbrook Av, Cherry, Milton, Campbell, Elm Av, Farrell Pl (now part of Broad Street), Irving, Broad, Fulton, Vail Pl. One part.

sheet-5-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 5 is the main map, at 50 feet to an inch, with north pointing to the top and slightly to the right. It lies on the north side of the centre of Rahway between Campbell Street at the left and Main Street at the right, with Irving Street running down the middle. Central Avenue crosses the top; Coach Street, Elizabeth Avenue and Elm Avenue cross the sheet below it, and Poplar Street runs along the bottom beside the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks at the lower right. Stores fill the east side of Irving Street at its upper end, including the Rahway Theatre. The block between Campbell Street and Irving Street holds rows of stores, the Y.M.C.A. with its gymnasium, swimming pool and bowling alleys, the Craftsmens Club with a post office and Masonic lodge, the Empire Theatre, the Evangelical Lutheran Zion Church, the Public Service Electric and Gas Company showroom and small dwellings. East of Irving, the Rahway Clothing Company, a battery and tire service, a drug store, an electric printing shop, a large garage, and dwellings, with a block of dwellings and stores below Elm Avenue. The lower left corner of the sheet is taken by an inset, part 2. Neighbouring sheets 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 18 are indicated in the margins.
notes: Central is Central Avenue and Main is West Main Street in OpenStreetMap.
The Y.M.C.A. is lettered Railway Y.M.C.A. beside Irving Street.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts. Part 1: Central Av, Hamilton, Campbell, Irving, Coach, Elizabeth Av, Elm Av, Main, Poplar. Part 2: inset in the lower left, the Mac-Lac-Kasebier-Chatfield shellac works by the Rahway River on Lawrence Street; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Mac-Lac-Kasebier-Chatfield shellac works by the Rahway River on Lawrence Street (no street junction and no feature shared with a placed neighbour; needs hand-picked control (parcel corners or imagery) near Lawrence Street and the river).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the district north-west of the centre of Rahway at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right. Hamilton Street runs diagonally down the left of the sheet and Seminary runs parallel to it through the middle, with Oliver, a 40 foot street that is drawn offset where it meets Hamilton and Seminary, across the top and Gordon Place cutting between Hamilton and Seminary below. Irving Street comes in from the lower right and W. Grand forms the right side of the sheet. The blocks are lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots with house numbers. Larger buildings are the Jr. O.U.A.M. lodge rooms near the top, a vacant building and a large brick works on Seminary, the Rahway Library and the German Evangelical Church near the right, and St. Mark's German Catholic Church in the lower middle. Below Gordon Place stands the Hamilton Laundry Inc., a pants factory, and the Atomizer Corp'n, makers of electric spraying machines. The Rahway River (Robinson's Branch) crosses the lower left in blue and the Elizabethtown Consolidated Gas Co. occupies the bank opposite, with a gas holder, a meter house and a pipe shop. Central Avenue runs along the bottom edge. Neighbouring sheets 5, 7 and 18 are indicated in the margins.
notes: Oliver is offset by about 50 feet at Hamilton Street; the modern node was taken on the eastern part of the street.
Gordon Place and Seminary were hand-picked at the pipe crossing.
Hamilton is Hamilton Street, Seminary is Seminary Avenue, Irving is Irving Street and W. Grand is West Grand Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Map, 50 ft. Oliver, West Grand, Seminary, Gordon Pl, Hamilton, Irving, Central Av, Main, Robinson's Branch. One part. Gordon Pl / Seminary hand-picked.

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 7 is the central business and residential district of Rahway where Irving, Main and West Grand meet the Rahway River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Irving runs diagonally from the left edge up to the top centre, crossed by Seminary Avenue; below the bend of the river it continues as Main, which carries a continuous row of two and three storey stores and dwellings from Central Avenue down to Elizabeth Avenue at the bottom, with Coach Street entering from the west. Along Main are a hay and feed store, a glass works and framing shop, an undertaker, a plumbing and tin shop, and an insurance office, with a drug store at the head of Irving. West Grand runs from the top of the sheet down to the right, lined with dwellings, and carries the German Evangelical Lutheran Church; Newton, Union and Allen are the cross streets in the upper right, where narrow lots hold small frame houses, sheds and a few barns. The Rahway River, Robinson's Branch and the North Branch cross the sheet in broad curves, and Rahway River Park lies on the east bank near the bottom. Large unplotted blocks are marked 5, 6, 18, 21 and 28, the numbers of adjoining sheets. A compass rose at the upper left shows the turned orientation, and the scale bar sits at the bottom. The lower right is cut off by the heavy border of the inset (part 2). Water pipes of 4, 8, 10 and 12 inches are drawn along the streets.
notes: Main is West Main Street in OpenStreetMap, Irving is Irving Street, West Grand is West Grand Avenue.
Union and the east end of Newton do not survive as streets in the modern network, so no control was taken east of West Grand.
Control rests on five junctions (Irving / Seminary Avenue, Newton / West Grand, Allen / West Grand, Coach Street / Main, Elizabeth Avenue / Main); the right half of the part has none.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts. Part 1: Irving, Seminary Av, Main, Central Av, Coach, Elizabeth Av, West Grand, Newton, Union, Allen, Rahway River. Part 2: inset in the lower right, Three in One Oil Co. at Elizabeth Av and Lincoln Av (anchored on one hand-picked junction).

sheet-7-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 7 is an inset in the lower right showing the works of the Three in One Oil Co., makers of lubricating oil, between Elizabeth Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, and is bounded on its upper side by a heavy double line that cuts diagonally across the sheet. Elizabeth Avenue runs along the top of the inset and Lincoln Avenue runs down its right side, with a water main marked in both. The oil company's plant fills the block: a large concrete-floored storage building, a steel-frame store house, oil storage and oil compounding rooms, a coal bin, a packing department, a bottling department, a shipping room and an office, with a general manufacturing building of fireproof construction beside them. A wooden platform runs along the railroad at the lower edge, where the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks are marked. Two small dwellings stand in the open ground north of the plant. Notes on the sheet give the plant's fire protection: watchman, no clock, steam heat and lights and power, an inside hydrant with hose, chemical extinguishers, fire pails and sand pails. The adjoining blocks are numbered 21 and 28, and the strip below the plant is numbered 22 for the neighbouring sheet.
notes: The inset is placed from one hand-picked point at Elizabeth Avenue and Lincoln Avenue (West Lincoln Avenue in OpenStreetMap), with scale and rotation taken from the sheet; low confidence.
The inset covers the lower right of the sheet and is drawn at its own orientation, about 8 degrees from the main part.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts. Part 1: Irving, Seminary Av, Main, Central Av, Coach, Elizabeth Av, West Grand, Newton, Union, Allen, Rahway River. Part 2: inset in the lower right, Three in One Oil Co. at Elizabeth Av and Lincoln Av (anchored on one hand-picked junction).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the Rahway River crossing east of the centre of Rahway, at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right. Main Street runs down the left edge and the river, with a second branch of its channel drawn in blue, passes through the middle of the sheet. Elizabeth Avenue crosses the top, W. Grand runs down at the right, and Essex and Clarkson Place enter from the bottom, with Monroe along the lower edge. The Pennsylvania Railroad main line crosses the sheet diagonally with several tracks, passing above Bridge. North of the tracks stand the Miller and Hoff Lumber Co. with its sawing and planing mill, drive storage and lumber piles, The Wheatena Co. with a brick works and a gray warehouse, and Oliver Co. Inc., coal and mason's materials, with its car sheds and trestle. On the left bank of the river, along Main Street, stand a police garage and police station, the Exempt Firemen's Home, a plumber, electric printing and stores. South of the tracks are The White Ice and Coal Co. Inc., makers of artificial ice, the Rahway Laundry Inc., the Rahway Sub. Sta. of the Public Service Electric and Gas Co., a junk store and dwellings along Essex. Neighbouring sheets 2, 5, 7, 21, 22 and 23 are indicated in the margins.
notes: Main is West Main Street north of Poplar Street and Main Street to the south in OpenStreetMap; Bridge is Bridge Street, Essex is Essex Street and W. Grand is West Grand Avenue.
The river is lettered Rahway River in pieces across the sheet.
Map, 50 ft. Main, Elm Av, Poplar, Bridge, Monroe, Clarkson Pl, Dock, Essex, West Grand, Elizabeth Av, Rahway River, PRR. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows an industrial district on the east side of Rahway, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. East Scott Avenue runs along the top, East Grand Avenue along the bottom, and Montgomery runs down the right edge between them, with Lawrence Street leaving East Grand at the lower right. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs down the left edge, with a freight house, coal bins and the yards of two coal and ice dealers beside it near the bottom. The centre is taken up by the works of the Royal Manufacturing Co., cotton and wool waste, a group of brick-walled buildings with a power house, shipping department, ware houses, picker and mixer rooms, a wash room and a drying room, with offices and a garage in front, a 54,000 gallon cistern and a private spur and sidings that curve across the open ground to the north. The Hamilton Mfg Co. ware house, making dentists' and printers' furniture, stands in the upper left. Along the right edge, between East Scott Avenue and East Grand Avenue, narrow lots on Montgomery hold small frame dwellings, with a large storage shed at the works boundary and the Elks Home (I.B.P.O.E.) near the bottom. A recreation house stands south of the works. The works notes give construction, fire protection, watchman and water supply. Large blocks are numbered 21 and 22 for neighbouring sheets, and block numbers 53, 54, 59 and 60 appear in the interior. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and an 8 inch main on East Grand Avenue are marked.
notes: East Grand is East Grand Avenue and Montgomery is Montgomery Street in OpenStreetMap.
Control is three junctions (East Scott Avenue / Montgomery, East Grand Avenue / Montgomery, East Grand Avenue / Lawrence Street), so the fit is exact; low confidence.
Lawrence Street is not drawn north of East Grand Avenue, so East Scott Avenue / Lawrence Street is not available.
Map, 50 ft. East Scott Av, East Grand, Montgomery, Lawrence; factory grounds (Regina Manufacturing area) and rail sidings. One part; only three junctions (exact fit).

sheet-10-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 10 is the lower half of the sheet, below the heavy line, showing the area south of East Milton Avenue between Main and the Rahway River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper left. West Milton Avenue meets Main at the upper left, and East Milton Avenue runs from Main to the river along the top of the part. Main runs down the left side, with a telephone exchange on the corner of Milton and a row of brick and frame dwellings and stores, a paper and twine shop among them, facing it; the ground west of Main is left blank for sheet 3. Along East Milton Avenue stand a public garage for 25 cars, a long row of attached two-storey frame dwellings (nos. 29 to 51) and the 2nd Baptist Church (Colored); a few dwellings and a shed stand by the river bank at the east end. The interior of the large blocks 128 and 129 is mostly open, with garages, the waste paper business of Joseph Mancuso and storage buildings. Haydock runs along the bottom edge, with small frame dwellings and garages on its north side, and long narrow lots run down to it from the middle of the part. At the right edge, beside the river, is the City Incinerator Plant, of brick with concrete floors and furnaces, reached by a ramp. Water pipes are drawn along the streets and a 50 ft scale bar is printed at the bottom.
notes: Main is Main Street and both Miltons are East Milton Avenue in OpenStreetMap at this junction; Haydock is not in OpenStreetMap.
Works of note: telephone exchange, public garage, 2nd Baptist Church (Colored), Joseph Mancuso waste paper dealer, City Incinerator Plant.
Placed from one detected junction (East Milton Avenue / Main) with rotation from its drawn lines and the 50 ft scale assumed: low confidence away from that corner.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (upper): American Felt Co. Essex Mill on Westfield Road, 'located about 2 miles N.W. of P.O.', with mill pond and Rahway River; no street junction. Part 2 (lower): E. Milton Av, W. Milton Av, Main, Haydock, city incinerator plant; E. and W. Milton drawn offset at Main.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: American Felt Co. Essex Mill on Westfield Road, about 2 miles northwest of the post office (no street junction; Westfield Road, a mill pond and the Rahway River only, probably outside the reference box in Clark; needs locating the mill site and hand-picked control).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows a residential district in the south-west of Rahway, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. West Hazelwood Avenue runs down the left side, Maple Avenue down the middle and Commerce down the right, crossed by Bryant at the top, Jaques Avenue through the middle and Broad along the railroad at the bottom. The four large blocks are filled with frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, mostly with a small outbuilding behind, on lots running back from the street, with house numbers marked along the frontages. Several blocks have large open areas behind the frontages, and one brick-walled building stands among the houses of the upper left block. Along the bottom the sheet is crossed by the tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad, drawn with a long concrete wall on the north side and many parallel tracks, with the scale bar printed over the right-of-way. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 12 inches run down the streets, with fire hydrants, telephone and fire alarm boxes marked, and street widths of 60 and 66 feet are noted. The neighbouring sheets are indicated by the numbers 13 and 15 at the sides, 26 below the railroad and 3 at the lower right, and the printed block numbers 488, 489, 492 and 493 stand in the middle of each block.
notes: Jaques Avenue is Jacques Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Maple Avenue and Bryant are Maple Avenue and Bryant Street.
Commerce is West Emerson Avenue in OpenStreetMap: it was checked against the fit from the other streets, where the two junctions at Jaques Avenue and Broad fall on the drawn street.
The Pennsylvania Railroad at the bottom is not used for control.
Map, 50 ft. West Hazelwood Av, Maple Av, Bryant, Jaques Av, Broad, Commerce (West Emerson Avenue), Georgia. One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers a thinly built residential district in the southwest of Rahway, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. St. George's Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, and the long blocks on either side run at an angle to the page, bounded by Madison Avenue at the upper left, Plainfield Avenue, Orchard, Inman Avenue, Jefferson Avenue, Grove, Sycamore and Meadow Avenue. Below St. George's Avenue the blocks between Albermarle Avenue, Beverly, Tehema, Murray and Remsen are cut by narrow wedges where streets meet at sharp angles. In the lower part of the sheet Jaques Avenue runs straight across, with Murray, Adele, Plainfield Avenue, Minna, Inman Avenue and Coddington crossing it, and Pierpont and Bryant run to the right of St. George's Avenue. The Pennsylvania Railroad main line occupies the bottom edge, with its bank of parallel tracks drawn across the full width. Most lots are long and narrow and still empty; the houses are frame dwellings, with a few garages and sheds. Near St. George's Avenue at Beverly and Plainfield Avenue there are small automobile repair premises with gasoline tanks, and a short row of dwellings with outbuildings stands on Jefferson Avenue between Inman and Grove. Water pipes are drawn as dashed lines in the streets, and the printed street widths are 50, 60, 66 and 80 feet. Block numbers run from 556 to 639. The sheet is bordered by sheets 13, 16, 25 and 28, which are named at its edges.
notes: Jaques Avenue is Jacques Avenue in OpenStreetMap. Inman Avenue is West Inman Avenue, Orchard is Orchard Street, Murray is Murray Street, Grove is Grove Street, Sycamore is Sycamore Street, Minna is Minna Street, Adele is Adele Street, Coddington is Coddington Street and Albermarle is Albermarle Street.

The street drawn as Meadow Avenue at the upper right is West Meadow Avenue today; the vertical street drawn as Meadow beside sheet 13 is Forbes Street in OpenStreetMap (matched on the junctions with Bryant and Jacques Avenue).
Beverly, Tehema and Remsen west of Murray were left out of the control; they are not matched to modern streets.
The Pennsylvania Railroad main line at the bottom is drawn about 18 m from its modern line; the rail crossings were not used as control.

Map, 100 ft. Southwest: St. George's Av, Inman Av, Plainfield Av, Orchard, Coddington, Minna, Adele, Murray, Albermarle Av, Jaques Av. One part. The vertical 'Meadow' beside sheet 13 is Forbes Street today.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers a residential district in the southwest of Rahway, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It runs from St. George's Avenue along the top edge down to the Pennsylvania Railroad main line at the bottom, and from Meadow Avenue on the left to West Hazelwood Avenue and Maple Avenue on the right. The cross streets Pierpont, Bryant and Jaques Avenue run across the sheet, and Walters, Oak, Lake Avenue, Stearns, Stanton and Albert run up it to St. George's Avenue. The blocks are filled with frame dwellings and garages on narrow lots, with house numbers along the frontages; many lots are still empty, especially in the upper left between St. George's Avenue, Stanley Place and Meadow Avenue, where only a few houses stand on large parcels. Roosevelt School stands in a large open block between St. George's Avenue and Pierpont, and the Roosevelt Apartments face Lake Avenue just below Pierpont. In the lower left, beside the railroad, is the works of the McNeill Cooperage Co., makers of barrels, with stave storage, kilns, a blacksmith shop and a long manufacturing building. Rahway Hospital, with its wards and heating plant, lies near West Hazelwood Avenue in the lower right. Broad Street runs along the railroad in the lower right part of the sheet. Water pipes are drawn as dashed lines down most streets, with street widths of 60 and 66 feet noted. Neighbouring sheets 4, 11, 12, 14, 15, 25, 26 and 28 are indicated by numbers in the margins.
notes: Jaques Avenue is Jacques Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Stearns is West Stearns Street, Albert is West Albert Street, Lake Avenue is West Lake Avenue and Meadow Avenue is West Meadow Avenue.
Albert is drawn offset at Jaques Avenue (the street north of Jaques lies about 100 ft west of the part south of it); it was left out of the control.
Works of note: McNeill Cooperage Co. (barrels), Roosevelt School, Roosevelt Apartments, Rahway Hospital.

Map, 100 ft. Southwest residential district: St. George's Av, Pierpont, Bryant, Jaques Av (Jacques Avenue), Broad; Walters to W. Hazelwood and Maple Av. One part. Pilot sheet (28 points, LOO 1.2 m). Albert drawn offset at Jaques, left out.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the west side of Rahway along the Rahway River and Robinson's Branch, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. The upper half is mostly undeveloped land cut into large numbered blocks (400, 432, 469, 495, 498, 504) by streets marked Not Opened, with Warren, Madison Avenue and Milton Boulevard drawn as paper streets; only a few dwellings stand on Milton Boulevard. The river enters at the upper left, winds under an iron bridge at Madison Avenue and a concrete bridge at Jefferson Avenue, and bends sharply near St. George's Avenue before joining Robinson's Branch at the right edge. Old Lake Avenue crosses diagonally, and West Hazelwood Avenue, Maple Avenue, Milton, Elm and Central Avenue run across the page between Madison and Jefferson Avenue. Streets of narrow lots lie between Beverly Place, Lincoln Place and Nicholas Place, with a closely built row of dwellings on Nicholas Place and Central Avenue. The principal industry is greenhouse growing: Brumann Bros., Florists, with three long greenhouses on the left, and J. R. Brumann, Florist, and C. E. Brumann, Inc., Florist, between Race and Jefferson Avenue, with heating plants. The Kant-Rust Product Corp. (packing and shipping) stands at Cross, and a garage and a group of small stores line St. George's Avenue near Maple. Large blocks 455, 456 and 440 beside the river hold only a few buildings. Water pipes of 6, 10 and 12 inches are drawn, and street widths of 33 to 80 feet are noted. Sheets 13, 15, 16, 28 and 29 adjoin.
notes: Milton Boulevard, Old Lake Avenue, Central Avenue, Maple Avenue, Nicholas Place, Mooney Place and Charlotte Place keep their names in OpenStreetMap. Cross is Cross Street, Race is Race Street and West Hazelwood Avenue keeps its name.
Warren, Beverly Place and Lincoln Place are not in OpenStreetMap; the streets marked Not Opened were never built on these lines.
Sheet drawn turned about 79 degrees clockwise; fitted scale 3.95 px/ft.
Map, 100 ft. West: Madison Av, Old Lake Av, Milton Blvd, Elm, Maple Av, Jefferson Av, Race, Cross, St. George's Av, Rahway River and Robinson's Branch; Baumann florists' greenhouses. One part.

sheet-15-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 15 is the main map of a residential district in central-west Rahway, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right at about 65 degrees. It runs from St. George's Avenue along the top to Esterbrook Avenue at the lower right, and from Maple Avenue on the left to Central Avenue on the right. Pierpont, Bryant Street and Jaques Avenue cross the sheet from left to right, while W. Milton Avenue, Elm Avenue, Commerce and Clinton run up and down it. Most of the blocks are built with frame dwellings, a number of them two-and-a-half storeys, with garages behind. Notable buildings include Lincoln School (brick, steam heated), the Ilderan Outing Club on Maple Avenue, a garage and repair shop with a show room at St. George's Avenue, the Woman's Club and the B.P.O.E. Club House near Jaques Avenue and Clinton, and a long row of attached brick dwellings along Bryant Terrace, with Maple Terrace behind. Streets are 50 to 66 feet wide, with water pipes of 2 to 10 inches drawn as dashed lines. A heavy line cuts off a lower-left inset of the sheet, drawn separately with its own north arrow; it is not part of this part and is not georeferenced. Neighbouring sheets 3, 4, 11, 13, 14, 16 and 18 are named at the edges.
notes: Jaques Avenue is Jacques Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Pierpont is Pierpont Street, Clinton is Clinton Street, W. Milton Avenue is West Milton Avenue, and Cherry Street is West Cherry Street or East Cherry Street today.
Commerce, as drawn between Bryant Street and Jaques Avenue, is not a street name in OpenStreetMap and was not used as control.
The inset in the lower-left corner (Commerce, Clinton and Georgia, with its own north arrow) is not georeferenced; see the sheet note.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1: St. George's Av, Pierpont, Maple Av, West Milton Av, Elm Av, Central Av, Bryant, New Church, Esterbrook Av. Part 2: small inset in the lower left (Commerce, Clinton, Georgia); not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: small inset in the lower left: Commerce, Clinton and Georgia (ground location uncertain (the main part already draws Clinton / Georgia); Commerce not in OpenStreetMap; needs step 6b carry from sheet 3 or 11).

sheet-16-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 16 is the main map of a sparsely built district in the west of Rahway, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right at about 78 degrees. Jefferson Avenue runs along the top, Central Avenue down the left edge and Hamilton down the right, with St. George's Avenue crossing the middle of the sheet. Between Central Avenue and Stone, Mooney Place divides two rows of small frame dwellings on narrow lots. South of it Robinson's Branch enters at the left and joins the Rahway River, which passes under St. George's Avenue, curves down through the lower left and runs under a bridge at New Church. The large blocks 895 and 896 in the centre are mostly open ground with a few farm-style houses and outbuildings. Church runs down the middle of the lower half, with a close row of small houses on its west side, and Miller's Lane and Fornote branch off to the east. A few lots on Hamilton and Trussler Place are laid out with houses along their frontage. A heavy line marks off an inset at the lower right with its own north arrow and a different set of streets (Leesville Avenue, Remsen, Murray); that inset is not part of this part and is not georeferenced. Street widths of 50 to 80 feet are marked, and the sheet is bordered by sheets 12, 14, 15, 17, 18 and 29.
notes: Stone is Stone Street, Church is Church Street, Hamilton is Hamilton Street and Fornote is Fernote Street in OpenStreetMap; Miller's Lane is Millers Lane.
The inset at the lower right (Leesville Avenue, Remsen, Murray, St. George's Avenue) is not georeferenced; see the sheet note.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1: Jefferson Av, Mooney Pl, Stone, Central Av, St. George's Av, Church, Fornote (Fernote Street), Miller's Lane, Hamilton, Robinson's Branch. Part 2: inset in the lower right at Leesville Av, Remsen, Murray and St. George's Av near the PRR; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset in the lower right: Leesville Av, Remsen, Murray, St. George's Av and the PRR (drawn spacing does not match the modern junctions; location uncertain; needs step 6b from sheet 12).

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the northern edge of Rahway, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. The upper half is thinly built. Along the top, Madison Avenue and Clark run across the sheet, and the Rahway Water Works (municipal) stands at the top right beside the North Branch of the Rahway River, with a suction well, filter house, pump house and two large circulating basins and stand pipes drawn in plan; a printed note describes the works and its daily consumption. Rahway Cemetery fills the large open ground in the centre and right, with a stone yard (T. Jardine and Son) and a stone cutting shed near its southern gate. On the left, small frame dwellings line Fowler Place, Brown Place, Jefferson Avenue and Trussler Place, and larger dwellings stand along Hamilton, Westfield Avenue and High, which converge toward St. George's Avenue. St. George's Avenue crosses the lower third of the sheet; the St. George Hotel, a fire alarm box and several automobile repair shops stand at its junction with Westfield Avenue and West Grand. Below it is a built-up district of frame dwellings and garages along Hamilton, Seminary, West Grand and Union, with the Church of the Holy Comforter, a pale blue building marked as heated by steam and lit by electricity, on Seminary. Fornote and Factory close the sheet at the bottom. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches are drawn as dashed lines in most streets, and street widths of 50, 60 and 66 feet are noted. Neighbouring sheets 16, 18, 19 and 29 are named in the margins.
notes: Modern names: Madison Avenue, Westfield Avenue, Hamilton Street, Seminary Avenue, West Grand Avenue, Union Street and Saint Georges Avenue (St. George's Avenue) are in OpenStreetMap; Clark and Harold Avenue are Clark Street and Harold Avenue.
Fornote, Factory and Water Works Lane are not in OpenStreetMap and gave no control.
A street at the top left is marked not opened.
Works of note: Rahway Water Works (municipal), Church of the Holy Comforter, St. George Hotel, T. Jardine and Son stone yard.
Map, 100 ft. North edge: Madison Av, Broadway, Harold Av, Westfield Av, St. George's Av, Seminary, West Grand, Union; water works and Rahway Cemetery. One part.

sheet-18-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 18, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. It covers the old centre of Rahway north-west of the downtown blocks, on both sides of Robinsons Branch, which crosses the left of the sheet in a blue channel. The notched mask leaves out the pentagon-shaped inset in the lower middle, which is part 2. The densest area is the grid of Hamilton, Seminary, West Grand and Union, crossed by Fornote and Factory at the top, Church in the middle and Oliver below it, with Whittier and Newton at the lower right. Frame dwellings and garages fill most blocks. Institutions include the First Presbyterian Church with its Community House and the First M.E. Church on West Grand, a fire department house on Seminary, and fire alarm boxes at several corners. Industry lies at the top and on the left: the Milbury-Atlantic works on Hamilton making bath robes and bathing suits, R. C. Grube's wagon and auto body works on Factory, with machine wood work and a blacksmith shop, and the United Body Corp. auto body works on New Church. A lodge home (F.O.E.) stands on Whittier. In the lower left the city playground, the Ebenezer A.M.E. Church and scattered houses lie along Central and Esterbrook Avenue, west of the stream. Millers Lane and Church run diagonally on the upper left. Water pipes of 6 inches are drawn as dashed lines in most streets, with street widths of 33, 40, 50, 60 and 66 feet noted. Neighbouring sheets 4, 5, 6, 7, 15, 16, 17, 19 and 21 are named in the margins.
notes: Church jogs about 30 m at West Grand and again at Union; both offsets are drawn and match OpenStreetMap, so each cross street has two junctions with Church.
Modern names: Hamilton Street, Seminary Avenue, West Grand Avenue, Union Street, Central Avenue, Esterbrook Avenue and New Church Street. Fornote and Factory are not in OpenStreetMap.
Works of note: Milbury-Atlantic (bath robes and bathing suits), R. C. Grube wagons and auto bodies, United Body Corp., First Presbyterian Church and Community House, First M.E. Church, F.O.E. Home.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1: Church, New Church, Hamilton, Seminary, West Grand, Union, Oliver, Whittier, Esterbrook Av, City Playground. Part 2: pentagon inset at Esterbrook Av, Central Av, Elm Av and Campbell (exact three-point fit).

sheet-18-2.description: Part 2 is the pentagon-shaped inset in the lower middle of sheet 18, outlined by a heavy double line and drawn at the same 100 feet to an inch and the same orientation as the main map, with its own north arrow at the lower left. It shows a compact institutional district. Esterbrook Avenue runs along its upper left edge and Central Avenue along its upper right, with Elm Avenue on the lower left and Campbell on the lower right. Rahway High School, with its auditorium, manual training shop and annexes, stands on the lower side facing Campbell. In the upper middle are the Parochial School, built in 1925, St. Mary's R.C. Church, a second parochial school marked not in use, a convent and a rectory. The First Baptist Church stands at the left. Frame dwellings line Esterbrook Avenue and Campbell, mostly small lots drawn with rear sheds, and a block of larger lots in the middle is numbered 448. Water pipes of 6 inches run in the surrounding streets. The numbers 4, 5, 6 and 15 outside the heavy line name the neighbouring sheets, and 18 inside it names this one. The inset is placed apart from the main map: its streets do not join the main part's streets across the heavy line, so it was fitted on its own junctions.
notes: Fitted on two or three junctions only (Esterbrook and Central, Elm and Campbell, Campbell and Central), with scale and rotation agreeing with part 1; no further cross streets are named inside the inset.
Modern names: Esterbrook Avenue, Central Avenue, Elm Avenue and Campbell Street.
Works of note: Rahway High School, St. Mary's R.C. Church and parochial schools, First Baptist Church.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1: Church, New Church, Hamilton, Seminary, West Grand, Union, Oliver, Whittier, Esterbrook Av, City Playground. Part 2: pentagon inset at Esterbrook Av, Central Av, Elm Av and Campbell (exact three-point fit).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the north-central part of Rahway on both sides of the North Branch of the Rahway River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. St. George's Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet and the river, with the river bending to the south through the middle and a long island visible east of Factory Lane. On the left bank are the grid blocks between Union and Jackson Avenue, crossed by Factory Street, Ludlow, Church and Oliver. The Franklin Public School, with auditorium and gymnasium, and the older Franklin School stand in this district, and the greenhouses of two florists, Lena M. Saling and J. W. Saling, occupy blocks on Jackson Avenue and Union. A weed killer manufactory stands on Union at the left. On the bank beside the river, between Factory Lane and St. George's Avenue, stands a vacant tile works with its boiler house. On the east bank River and West Scott Avenue run down the page past large undivided tracts, with houses scattered along them and a tight row of small dwellings and a fire alarm box on River View Place at the lower right. The top of the sheet is the Rahway River Parkway of the Union County Park System, with the Rahway Cemetery at the upper left, a Marsh Estate at the upper right and a few farm sheds. Dashed lines show 4 to 10 inch water pipes, and street widths of 30 to 66 feet are noted. Neighbouring sheets 17, 18, 20 and 21 are named in the margins.
notes: Church jogs about 30 m at Union and at West Scott Avenue; both offsets are drawn.

Modern names: Union Street, Harrison Street, Jackson Avenue, West Scott Avenue, Evans Street and River Road (River). Factory Street, Factory Lane and Gibby are not in OpenStreetMap; River View Place was not tied to a modern street.
Works of note: Franklin Public School, Franklin School, Lena M. Saling and J. W. Saling florists, a weed killer manufactory, a vacant tile works.

Map, 100 ft. Both banks of the North Branch: St. George's Av, Union, Harrison, Jackson Av, Ludlow, Church, Oliver, River (River Road), West Scott Av; Rahway River Parkway and Rahway Cemetery. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the north-east of Rahway between St. George's Avenue and the lower sheet edge, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. St. George's Avenue crosses the upper third of the sheet, and Maurice Avenue runs up from it at the upper left between rows of small frame dwellings. Most of the sheet is sparsely built. Large numbered tracts sit between the streets, with a few houses and outbuildings on them: Pine Lodge on St. George's Avenue, a group of co-operative sheds and farm buildings at the top centre, and scattered dwellings along Ross at the top right. Lincoln Avenue and Kearny Avenue are laid out as parallel streets into the middle of the sheet with long, narrow lots drawn on them, while Factory and Ludlow are marked not opened, with dashed street lines. Linden Avenue runs diagonally from the upper right to the lower left, with houses on its eastern side and Messenger's Laundry, steam heated and electrically powered, near its lower end. Building has concentrated in the lower left, where Church, Evans and Oliver are crossed by Thomas Place, Elinor Place, Dembling Place and Lincoln Avenue, with rows of identical frame dwellings and garages on small lots. West Scott Avenue forms the left edge. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches are drawn as dashed lines, and street widths of 30 to 66 feet are noted. Neighbouring sheets 19, 21 and 28 are named in the margins.
notes: Lincoln Avenue is West Lincoln Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Kearny Avenue, Linden Avenue, Maurice Avenue, Thomas Place and Elinor Place keep their names; Evans is Evans Street, Ross is Ross Street, and Church is Church Street.
Factory is not in OpenStreetMap, and Ludlow is drawn not opened here, so neither was used for control; Dembling Place is not in OpenStreetMap.
The fit is looser than other sheets (RMSE about 2.3 m); the junctions along West Scott Avenue and Linden Avenue sit 3 to 5 m off the fit.
Works of note: Pine Lodge, Messenger's Laundry.
Map, 100 ft. Northeast: St. George's Av, Maurice Av, Ross, West Scott Av, Church, Ludlow, Lincoln Av, Kearny Av, Linden Av, Evans. One part; sparse, weakest full sheet.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the north-central part of Rahway on both sides of the North Branch of the Rahway River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Whittier crosses the sheet near the top on a bridge over the river, with Oliver above it; Allen, Price and Elizabeth Avenue run across the lower half, and Broad and the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks form the bottom edge. West of the river, Union, Harrison and Cottage Place carry dwellings on narrow lots, with Newton and Allen below. The river and its branches wind through the centre, enclosing a large undeveloped tract between Gibby and Newton, where Newton is marked not open. East of the river West Scott Avenue runs down the middle, and Linden Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, with Jackson Avenue joining it near the river. The upper right is laid out in long blocks of small frame houses along Prospect, Waite Avenue, Morton Avenue and Allen, with Lincoln Avenue at the right edge. Industry appears along the bottom: the Whertena Co. cereal factory (built 1908 and 1913), the Quinn and Boden Co. printers, electrotypers and binders, a tile machine shop, the Evans Constn Co. lumber and mill, and J. C. Wheeler and Sons, electroplating. A scale bar for 100 feet to an inch is printed in the lower right. The numbers 7, 8, 9, 18, 19, 20, 22 and 28 mark neighbouring sheets, and the large numbers in the blocks (260 to 391) are block numbers.
notes: West Scott Avenue is the modern West Scott Avenue; Waite Avenue, Morton Avenue and Linden Avenue keep their names; the other streets are named Street or Avenue in OpenStreetMap (Oliver Street, Harrison Street, Whittier Street, Allen Street, Price Street, Prospect Street, Union Street, Newton Street, Cottage Street for Cottage Place).
Lincoln Avenue at the right edge is not used: its modern line (West Lincoln Avenue, 90 ft wide) lies 13 m from the drawn street.
Union Street north of Whittier Street does not follow its modern line (Oliver / Union rejected at 18 m).
The Pennsylvania Railroad at the bottom is drawn about 18 m from its modern line and is not used for control.
The channel in the upper centre is labelled with a river name that could not be read with certainty and is left out of the place names.

Map, 100 ft. Oliver, Harrison, Union, Newton, Whittier, Jackson Av, Prospect, Linden Av, West Scott Av, Waite Av, Morton Av, Allen, Price, Elizabeth Av, Broad. One part. West Lincoln Avenue left out (modern line 13 m off).

sheet-22-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 22 is the main map of the east side of Rahway between the Pennsylvania Railroad and Park Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. East Scott Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, crossed by Montgomery, Bond, Lufberry and Rutherford, with Lincoln Avenue along the right edge and East Grand Avenue curving down the left. At the top, Broad runs along the wide band of Pennsylvania Railroad tracks, and below them stands the large saw-tooth-roofed plant of Merck and Company, manufacturing chemists, with a private street named Lawrence and another marked Private St. on its east side. The lower blocks are regular rows of small frame dwellings on narrow lots, with house numbers along the frontages; Upton Place and Underhill Place are short streets between Bond and Lufberry, and the lower right is laid out in long lots in blocks numbered 32 to 37. A chapel (Grand Street Chapel) stands at the left edge on Montgomery, and an auto painting shop and a few small works are scattered among the dwellings. A wedge-shaped inset, bounded by a heavy line, is cut out of the upper left corner (part 2). The block numbers 62, 63, 65, 66, 68, 26, 29, 34, 36 and 37 are printed in the interiors, and the neighbouring sheets are given as 2, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13, 21, 23 and 24.
notes: Street names in OpenStreetMap: East Scott Avenue (West Scott Avenue north of the railroad), East Grand Avenue, Montgomery Street, Bond Street, Lufberry Street, Rutherford Street, Underhill Place.
Lawrence (private) is not used for control; Lincoln Avenue and Upton Place were not identified with a modern street and are not used.
Lufberry Street / Underhill Place was excluded (3.9 m residual on a narrow arm).
The Pennsylvania Railroad at the top is not used for control.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1: West and East Scott Av, Broad, Montgomery, Bond, Lufberry, Rutherford, Lincoln Av, Upton Pl, Underhill Pl, East Grand. Part 2: wedge inset at Bridge, Essex, Lawrence, Monroe, Montgomery and East Grand.

sheet-22-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 22 is a wedge-shaped inset in the upper left corner showing a district around Essex, Lawrence, Monroe and Montgomery, and the part of East Grand Avenue that bounds it on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, as shown by a compass at its lower edge, and is bounded on the right and below by a heavy double line. Essex runs diagonally up the left side and Bridge crosses the top, where a water pipe is marked. Lawrence and Montgomery run in parallel from lower left to upper right across the inset, crossed by Monroe, and East Grand Avenue runs down its right side. The blocks are filled with frame dwellings on narrow lots, among them a row of houses fronting Essex and another along East Grand Avenue, and a dwelling group on Lawrence that includes the Washington Public School, a brick building with a tower, with annexes beside it. The wedge is cut from the sheet; the blank areas beside it, numbered 8, 9 and 23, belong to neighbouring sheets, and 80, 81 and 82 are block numbers. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches and street widths of 66 feet are marked.
notes: Street names in OpenStreetMap: Bridge Street, Essex Street, Lawrence Street, Monroe Street, Montgomery Street, East Grand Avenue.
The inset is turned about 49 degrees, the same as the main part of the sheet, but is placed separately because the heavy line cuts it from the main part.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1: West and East Scott Av, Broad, Montgomery, Bond, Lufberry, Rutherford, Lincoln Av, Upton Pl, Underhill Pl, East Grand. Part 2: wedge inset at Bridge, Essex, Lawrence, Monroe, Montgomery and East Grand.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the east side of Rahway between the Rahway River and Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the top. The river bends down the left edge in a broad blue channel, with Dock and Lewis Street on its west side holding a city yard and a pale pink works, and Clarkson Place cutting in at the top left. The grid of Essex, Lenox Place, Lawrence, Columbus Place, Montgomery, Bond and Park runs from Monroe at the top down through Lafayette and Washington to East Milton Avenue and Hancock at the bottom. Houses and garages are concentrated on the frontages of Monroe, Lafayette and Washington at the top, with the large blocks numbered 97, 99, 101, 103 and 107 between Washington and East Milton Avenue divided into long narrow lots that were still empty. The Grover Cleveland Public School stands in the open block between Montgomery and Reeve, which is marked not opened, and Reeve and Columbus Place are drawn as dashed paper streets. East Grand Avenue crosses the top right, and State Highway Route No. 25, a wide road of about 100 feet, runs diagonally across the lower right past Park. South of East Milton Avenue the blocks hold rows of small dwellings on Johnson, Sherman and Totten, and narrow river lots at the lower left carry a small cemetery building. Water pipes of 2 to 8 inches are shown dashed, and street widths of 50, 60 and 66 feet are noted. Neighbouring sheets 2, 8, 10, 22, 24, 26 are named in the margins.
notes: East Grand is East Grand Avenue and State Highway Route No. 25 is US 1 in OpenStreetMap. Reeve is not in OpenStreetMap.
Essex Street at Washington lies about 5 m off the fit and was left out of the control.
Works of note: Grover Cleveland Public School, the city yard.

Map, 100 ft. East side: Monroe, Essex, Lafayette, Washington, Montgomery, Bond, Lenox Pl, Lawrence, Columbus Pl, Totten, East Milton Av, Hancock, Haydock, Rahway River, State Highway Route 25. One part.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the south-east part of Rahway between East Grand Avenue and the Rahway River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north at the top of the sheet, so that its streets read nearly square to the page. Washington and East Milton Avenue run across it, crossed by Park, Rutherford, Paterson, Turner, Lennington and Barnett. A broad diagonal belt, labelled State Highway and Route No 25, cuts across the middle from the lower left to the upper right, and East Grand Avenue and East Scott Avenue run on diagonals in the upper part, with Lyons, Teneyke Place, Upton Place and Paterson fanning out beside them. Most of the sheet is laid out in long narrow lots, many of them still without buildings, with frame dwellings concentrated along the street frontages and the blocks numbered 94, 109, 112, 115, 118, 121, 123, 146, 148 to 151. In the upper right, near Lennington and Lyons, a garage and an auto painting building stand beside a pink-coloured brick structure. Along the bottom the Rahway River widens across the sheet, with the Rahway Yacht Club and a boat dock on its bank, a city dock below Elm Place and a stream entering from the lower left near Hancock. Water pipes of 2, 4 and 6 inches are marked, with street widths of 50, 60, 64, 66 and 80 feet noted. A scale bar for 100 feet to an inch is printed at the bottom. Neighbouring sheets 22, 23, 47, 48, 124, 152 and 153 are indicated in the margins.
notes: Lennington is Lenington Street in OpenStreetMap; East Milton Avenue, East Scott Avenue and East Grand Avenue carry the same names; Washington, Rutherford, Park, Paterson and Barnett are Washington Street, Rutherford Street, Park Street, Paterson Street and Barnett Street.
State Highway Route No. 25 is US 1 in OpenStreetMap; its modern line is not used for control because the highway has been widened.
Elm Place, Hancock and Lafayette Street were read from the sheet but not identified with modern streets.
Control rests on 16 junctions of the street grid (Washington, East Milton Avenue, East Grand Avenue and East Scott Avenue crossed by Park, Rutherford, Paterson, Turner, Lennington and Barnett).

Map, 100 ft. East: Washington, Rutherford, Park, Paterson, Teneyke Pl, Upton Pl, East Scott Av, Lennington (Lenington Street), Barnett, East Grand, Turner, East Milton Av, Route 25, Rahway River. One part.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the southern edge of central Rahway, between the Pennsylvania Railroad yards at the top and the South Branch of the Rahway River at the bottom. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right at about 50 degrees. The top of the sheet is taken up by the railroad: tracks, a siding and the P.R.R. Freight House (brick) on New Brunswick Avenue, and the coal and supplies yard of Ellis Dow. The principal industrial site is Richard Hamilton, Inc., Export Cooperage, at Clarkson, a large frame works with shook sheds, whitewash and storage buildings, a machine shop and a siding from the railroad, with the Premier Oil and Gasol Supply Co. next to it. Rows of small frame dwellings fill the blocks between Meadow Avenue, Lake Avenue, Stearns and Albert, with Thorn, Turner Place and Elm Place crossing them; Main runs along the south side, with Mill meeting it from the west. On the left the blocks along Inman Avenue, Elizabeth, Charles and James are partly vacant. Below Main the river is drawn with a wide bend and two small bridges, with Leesville Avenue along the south side and unbuilt lots marked Not Named in the lower left. Water pipes are shown in nearly every street and widths of 35 to 66 feet are marked. Sheets 12, 13, 26 and 27 adjoin.
notes: Meadow Avenue is Regina Avenue in OpenStreetMap, Lake Avenue is East Lake Avenue, Stearns is East Stearns Street, Turner Place is Holly Place, Elm Place is Laurel Place and Inman Avenue is East Inman Avenue. These were matched by spacing along Main and New Brunswick Avenue.
Albert was left out of the control because its modern equivalent is not a street the detector uses.
Streets drawn as Not Named in the lower left were never built.

Map, 100 ft. South: Inman Av, Elizabeth, Charles, James, Clarkson, New Brunswick Av, Meadow Av (Regina Avenue), Lake Av, Stearns, Thorn, Main, Mill, Leesville Av, Force St, South Branch of the Rahway River. One part; renamings by spacing.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the south-central part of Rahway between the Pennsylvania Railroad at the top and the South Branch of the Rahway River at the bottom. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right at about 56 degrees. New Brunswick Avenue crosses the middle from left to right and Main runs along the lower part, first straight along the left and then bending to run diagonally up to the right. Streets between them include Iva, E. Hazelwood Avenue, William, Adams and Commerce, with Fulton above and Thorn and Hazel Place below. The district is closely built with frame dwellings, many with small outbuildings. The largest works is the National Pneumatic Co., makers of trolley and subway equipment, a brick plant with boiler house, machine shop and sprinkler system at the upper left; the Columbian Public School stands on E. Hazelwood Avenue, the 2nd Presbyterian Church on Main at Adams, and a pottery and a row of attached brick or stone buildings along Main. George M. Friese's farm implements, building materials and coal yard stands beside the river. Near the right edge the map shows only a few scattered buildings on large lots. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 12 inches are drawn along the streets, and widths of 33 to 66 feet are marked. A switch tower stands beside the railroad. Sheets 3, 10, 11, 13, 23, 25 and 27 are named at the edges.

sheet-27-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 27 covers the southeastern edge of Rahway south of the Rahway River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing slightly to the left of straight up. East Hazelwood Avenue runs along the top of the part, just below the river, with a row of brick-veneered two-storey dwellings and stores on its north side and the junctions of Leesville Avenue at the left and Lawrence Street and Woodbridge Road at the right, where Whelan Place leaves to the south. Below it the part is almost entirely open land divided into a few large numbered lots (761, 762, 763, 774, 778, 782, 786, 790). Edgar Road, marked as State Highway Route No. 25 with a concrete ramp, runs down the middle of the part; Leesville Avenue runs down its left edge with a handful of frame dwellings and a milk house; Force crosses the lower half diagonally, parallel to the heavy line that divides this part from the inset of the New Jersey Reformatory below; and Woodbridge Road runs down the right side with a short row of dwellings at its north end and a water pipe along it. Buildings elsewhere are scattered dwellings, garages and sheds. Most of the ground was evidently still farmland or vacant in 1929. A fire alarm box and a hydrant are marked at Hazelwood Avenue and Woodbridge Road. The part adjoins sheet 26 to the west and sheet 25 to the southwest.
notes: Edgar is labelled State Highway Route No. 25; it is US 1 (East Edgar Road) today and no longer meets East Hazelwood Avenue at grade, so it gave no control.
Force (Force Street on sheet 25) is not in OpenStreetMap; the ground it crossed is now built over.

sheet-28-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 28 is the upper half of the sheet, a residential district in the north of Rahway on the boundary with the City of Linden, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper left. It is bounded by Lincoln Avenue along the bottom, Donald Avenue and Jones Place along the top, Whittier on the left and Elizabeth Avenue on the right, with Allen and Price running up the middle and Kearney Avenue and Wilson Avenue crossing. The dash-dot line of the City of Linden boundary crosses the top of the part above Jones Place. The blocks are laid out in narrow numbered lots, many of them still empty; built lots carry one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages, densest along Allen, Price and Elizabeth Avenue and along the lower side of Wilson Avenue. West of Whittier the lots are drawn only in outline. In the upper right, beyond Elizabeth Avenue, stands the warehouse of W. A. Birdsall & Co., plumbing and heating supplies, with a pipe shed, and a broad strip of open ground (block 243) runs down the right side of the part beside a group of parallel lines at the sheet edge. Water pipes of 6 and 2 inches are drawn along the streets, and street widths of 50, 60 and 66 feet are noted. A heavy line along the bottom separates this part from the three insets drawn below it, which show other parts of the town.
notes: Kearney Avenue is Kearny Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Lincoln Avenue is West Lincoln Avenue.

sheet-28-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 28 is a narrow strip on the left side of the sheet showing the north end of Maurice Avenue in the north of Rahway, from the edge of sheet 20 up to the Clark Township city line. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper right. Maurice Avenue runs straight up the middle of the strip with a water pipe along it and hydrants at two points; it is the only street drawn, and the dash-dot line of the Clark Township boundary, marked City Line, crosses the top. On both sides the street is lined with narrow house lots in blocks 204 (west) and 200 (east), most of them built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages, house numbers running up to the 70s on the west side. Below the lowest buildings the lots are left blank, being drawn on sheet 20, whose number is printed in the street. Heavy lines on the right and bottom separate the strip from the Madison Avenue inset and the Tingley-Reliance rubber works inset.
notes: Placed from one point carried from sheet 20 (the hydrant in Maurice Avenue drawn on both sheets), with scale 4.0 px/ft and north 44 degrees assumed (sheet 20's rotation less the drawn lean of Maurice Avenue): low confidence.

sheet-28-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 28 is the largest inset on the lower part of the sheet, a residential district in the west of Rahway between Madison Avenue at the top and St. George's Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing to the right. Grove, Sycamore, Meadow Avenue and Lake Avenue run down the inset from Madison Avenue to St. George's Avenue, Jefferson Avenue crosses it, and Stanley Place runs from Jefferson Avenue to St. George's Avenue. The upper half, between Madison and Jefferson avenues, is mostly laid out in narrow numbered lots that are still empty, except for rows of small frame dwellings on Sycamore and Meadow Avenue and a few scattered houses, a barn and kennels in the large block between Meadow Avenue and Lake Avenue (block 546). Block 504, east of Lake Avenue, is almost empty but for a long single-storey building at the right edge and one house. Below Jefferson Avenue the blocks along Stanley Place and Lake Avenue are more closely built with one- and two-storey dwellings and garages. St. George's Avenue runs along the bottom edge, with water pipes, a hydrant and a fire alarm box marked. A scale bar is printed at the lower left, beside the heavy line that separates this inset from the Tingley-Reliance rubber works inset; another heavy line along the top separates it from part 1, and one on the left from the Maurice Avenue strip.
notes: Meadow Avenue is West Meadow Avenue in OpenStreetMap and Lake Avenue is West Lake Avenue.

sheet-28-4.description: Part 4 of sheet 28 is a small inset in the lower left corner of the sheet showing the works of the Tingley-Reliance Rubber Corp'n, makers of auto accessories and mechanical rubber goods, at Ross and St. George's Avenue in the north of Rahway near the Linden line. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper right. Ross runs down the left side of the inset and St. George's Avenue along the bottom. The rubber works occupy the middle of the block: an L-shaped brick building with a tire building, mill room, press room, make-up room, shipping room, office and machine shop, with a cement house and storage sheds nearby; a note records light and power by electricity, steam heat, extinguishers and pails and no watchman. To the right, in block 167, a group of long single-storey sheds stands in open ground. The lower part of the block, along St. George's Avenue, holds a few frame dwellings and garages numbered 15 to 27. Water pipes run along Ross and St. George's Avenue, with a hydrant and a fire alarm box at their junction. The number 20 printed in the inset marks the adjoining sheet. Heavy lines on its top and right sides separate it from the Maurice Avenue strip and the Madison Avenue inset.

sheet-29-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 29 covers the northwestern corner of Rahway along the boundary with Clark Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper right. Madison Hill Road runs along the top edge, with the dash-dot Clark Township city line crossing the upper right of the part. Kline Place crosses the left half, and Westfield Avenue runs down the middle from Madison Hill Road to its junction with Broadway and Madison Avenue near the bottom. East of Westfield Avenue a small grid of streets is laid out: Broadway running down, Harold Avenue along the right edge, and Franklin, Bedford, Lambert and Clarck crossing. Madison Avenue runs diagonally across the lower left, with the unopened ends of Stone and Hamilton Street meeting it, and a heavy line below it separates this part from the inset drawn in the lower right of the sheet. The left half, along Madison Hill Road and Kline Place, is divided into long narrow lots (blocks 858 to 861) with a row of one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages on each frontage; the large blocks below Kline Place (837, 862, 876) are open land. The blocks between Westfield Avenue and Harold Avenue (325 to 335) are laid out in house lots, a minority of them built with frame dwellings, many with garages. Water pipes of 2 to 6 inches are drawn along most streets, and widths of 50 to 80 feet are noted. The part adjoins sheet 17 at the bottom.
notes: Franklin, Bedford and Lambert are Franklin Street, Bedford Street and Lambert Street in OpenStreetMap.
Clarck, between Broadway and Harold Avenue, has no modern counterpart under that name in OpenStreetMap; it gave no control.
Stone and Hamilton Street are marked Not Open where they meet Madison Avenue.

sheet-29-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 29 is the inset in the lower right of the sheet, below the heavy line, showing a district in the west of Rahway between Madison Avenue and Jefferson Avenue. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing to the right. Madison Avenue runs across the top of the inset and Jefferson Avenue along the bottom; Central Avenue runs down the left side, Stone down the middle and Trussler Place down the right edge, and Thirza Place and Charlotte Place cross between Central Avenue and Stone. The blocks west of Stone (926, 927, 928) are closely built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages on narrow lots along Thirza Place and Charlotte Place, with house numbers on each lot. The large block east of Stone (883) is almost empty except for the new Memorial Hospital, drawn as a fireproof building of 1929 with protected steel frame, concrete floors and roof, tile and brick curtain walls and gypsum corridor walls, heated by steam and lit by electricity. A short row of dwellings stands along Trussler Place at the right edge (block 882). Water pipes run along Madison Avenue, Thirza Place and Jefferson Avenue, and street widths of 50 and 66 feet are noted. Numbers in the margin refer to the adjoining sheets 14, 16 and 17.
notes: Memorial Hospital, F. P. construction, built 1929.
Stone is Stone Street in OpenStreetMap. Today Stone Street jogs about 60 m at Madison Avenue; the node in line with the drawn street was used and the other excluded.
